name: Patscherkofel
kurzbeschreibung: Patscherkofel (2,248 m) is Innsbruck's iconic landmark mountain: modern 10-seater gondola, historic stone pine path (Zirbenweg), and Olympic runs.
preis: Hiking area freely accessible; Patscherkofelbahn cable car chargeable (Zirbenweg round-trip ticket available)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily mid-May to late October and December to April
beschreibung:
Overview

The distinctive, domed summit of Patscherkofel (2,248 m) stands as the cherished home mountain of Innsbruck and the defining landmark of the southern Inn Valley. Renowned as a two-time host venue of the Olympic Winter Games (1964 and 1976), the 'Kofel' with its prominent red summit telecommunications mast is a year-round outdoor paradise. Thanks to its sunny, south-facing orientation, the mountain offers exceptional hiking and leisure conditions throughout the seasons. Its gentle slopes are blanketed by ancient stone pine forests, representing one of the oldest and largest continuous stone pine stands in the entire alpine arch. From its panoramic terraces, visitors enjoy a 360-degree panorama encompassing Innsbruck, the limestone ramparts of the Nordkette, the Wipptal heading to the Brenner Pass, and the glistening glaciers of the Stubai and Zillertal Alps.

Route & Requirements

A modern, barrier-free 10-person gondola transports guests smoothly and quietly in ten minutes from the valley station in Igls up to the mountain terminal at 1,965 meters. Right outside the station begins the celebrated Zirbenweg: A gently undulating, expertly maintained panoramic trail leading through ancient stone pine woods to the Tulfeinalm on the Glungezer (walking time approx. 2.5 hours, difficulty T1, family-friendly). For summit seekers, a broad service road climbs in roughly one hour from the top station to the peak and the historic Patscherkofel summit house. Solid walking shoes and wind-protective jackets are recommended; the Zirbenweg can easily be navigated with all-terrain strollers.

Visit & Arrival

Reaching the valley station in Igls is remarkably straightforward: Municipal bus line J runs every ten minutes directly from Innsbruck Central Station to the Patscherkofelbahn. Motorists find ample parking at the base station, where parking fees are refunded upon purchasing a mountain lift ticket. The popular Zirbenweg circular ticket combines the Patscherkofelbahn, Glungezerbahn, and connecting buses into an affordable round trip.

Tips

Visit the University of Innsbruck's Alpine Garden right next to the top cable car station, showcasing more than 400 protected alpine plant species across two hectares. Watch the sunset from the terrace of the summit house before savoring regional delicacies at Restaurant Das Kofel.
